Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q3 FY24 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by the number of the line you'd like to ask the question from. There will be a brief audio prompt confirming your request. To withdraw your question, press star two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q3 FY24 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; and Lisa Wong, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q3 FY24. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our CloudForge AI Studio and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on four key areas: accelerating AI product innovation, enhancing customer retention and expansion, driving go-to-market efficiency, and generating robust free cash flow.

On AI innovation, we launched several key features in CloudForge AI Studio, including multimodal LLMs for autonomous data querying, which have already seen strong adoption among our enterprise customers, reducing query times by up to 50%.

In customer retention, our land-and-expand model continues to shine, with expansions offsetting any contractions and positioning us for sustained growth.

For go-to-market efficiency, we're seeing improving sales productivity and operating leverage as we scale.

And on cash flow, our SaaS model is delivering impressive margins, giving us firepower for reinvestment.

We'll dive deeper into these shortly. We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $152 million, representing a 34% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and non-GAAP operating income was $42 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

Let me now dive deeper into some key aspects of our performance, starting with our operating expense breakdown. I'm pleased to report that we delivered strong expense discipline while continuing to invest aggressively in our growth priorities. Total non-GAAP operating expenses came in at $131 million, representing 86% of revenue—down 900 basis points year-over-year from 95% in Q3 FY23, and a sequential improvement from 88% in Q2. This reflects the operating leverage inherent in our SaaS model as we scale toward our Rule of 40 target, with growth at 34% and adjusted operating margin expanding to 28%. Dollar-wise, op ex grew 15% YoY, well below our revenue growth rate, driven by efficiencies in sales productivity and G&A scaling.

Breaking this down by line item, starting with Research and Development, which totaled $46 million, or 30% of revenue—up 18% YoY in dollars but flat sequentially as a percentage of revenue. R&D remains our largest investment area, underscoring our commitment to product leadership in the enterprise AI analytics space. Key drivers here include a 22% headcount ramp in engineering, bringing our total R&D team to over 850 globally, with a focus on accelerating our GenAI roadmap. We've poured resources into our new ForgeAI Agent platform, which integrates multimodal LLMs similar to those powering Anthropic's Claude or OpenAI's GPT-4o, enabling autonomous data querying and predictive insights for customers like our Fortune 500 cohort.

Regionally, about 60% of R&D spend is US-based in our Seattle and Austin hubs, but we've doubled down on our Bangalore center, now accounting for 25% of the budget, to tap lower-cost talent for core ML model training and scalability work. This has helped us ship 15 major features this quarter, including zero-ETL integrations with Snowflake and Databricks, which boosted our net revenue retention to 118%. Looking ahead, we expect R&D to tick up to 31-32% of revenue in H2 as we invest in vertical-specific AI agents for healthcare and finance—think HIPAA-compliant workflows akin to Veeva's expansions—while maintaining our gross margins north of 78%.

Moving to Sales and Marketing, expenses were $56 million, or 37% of revenue—up just 12% YoY, but down 250 basis points as a percentage from last year. This is a testament to our go-to-market efficiency, with customer acquisition cost payback now at 14 months, improved from 18 months a year ago, and sales productivity per rep hitting $1.8 million in ARR, up 15%. Our efficient growth score—revenue growth divided by S&M spend—improved to 0.76x from 0.62x YoY, putting us in line with high performers like HubSpot or ServiceNow.

Strategically, we're shifting 40% of our S&M budget toward product-led growth and account-based marketing, targeting our ideal customer profile of enterprises with $500M+ revenue running hybrid cloud environments. Demand gen campaigns around ForgeAI have driven a 35% increase in pipeline from inbound leads, reducing reliance on paid channels. Regionally, US spend remains dominant at 65% or $36 million, fueling our 32% YoY ARR growth there amid strong hyperscaler partnerships with AWS and Azure. EMEA grew to 20% of the budget or $11 million, with notable wins in the DACH region via localized GDPR-compliant features, while APAC at 15% or $8 million is ramping through joint ventures in Japan and Australia, where we've seen 45% YoY bookings growth despite macro headwinds like yen depreciation. We expect S&M as a percentage to decline further to the mid-30s by year-end as our land-and-expand motion matures, with upsell NRR at 125%.

Finally, General and Administrative expenses were $29 million, or 19% of revenue—flat YoY in dollars and down 100 basis points as a percentage. This line is scaling beautifully with the business, as fixed costs like facilities and IT infrastructure dilute over our growing employee base of 2,100. Stock-based compensation here was $8 million, in line with peers at about 2.5% of revenue, and we've optimized professional fees through vendor consolidation. Regional commentary: 70% US-centric for compliance and exec functions, with EMEA/APAC efficiencies from our shared services model in Dublin and Singapore.

Key exclusions for non-GAAP: We adjusted for $12 million in SBC across op ex, primarily in R&D and S&M, and $3 million in restructuring from last year's workforce optimization. Overall, these trends position us well for 25%+ revenue growth in FY25 while expanding margins to 20%, mirroring the playbook of category leaders like Palantir in their enterprise AI pivot.

Next, I'd like to highlight our Rule of 40 score, a key benchmark that our investors and the SaaS community hold us to. For those new to our story, the Rule of 40—popularized by Bessemer Venture Partners and now a staple for public SaaS names like Snowflake, Datadog, and Monday.com—combines our year-over-year revenue growth rate with our free cash flow margin. The goal is a combined score of 40% or higher, balancing top-line momentum with disciplined profitability as we scale.

I'm pleased to report that for the trailing twelve months ended October 31st, CloudForge delivered a Rule of 40 score of 62%. This breaks down to 35% revenue growth—driven by robust ARR expansion—and a 27% FCF margin, reflecting our maturing operating leverage. Let me unpack this in detail.

First, on revenue growth: Our Q3 revenue came in at $152 million, up 34% year-over-year and slightly ahead of our guidance midpoint. This translates to trailing twelve-month revenue growth of 35%, fueled primarily by our ARR, which reached $525 million at quarter-end, up 36% YoY. Dollar-based net retention remained strong at 118%, underscoring our land-and-expand model. Customers like a Fortune 100 financial services firm expanded their deployment of our CloudForge DataMesh platform by 3x during the quarter, migrating additional workloads from legacy on-prem systems.

Regionally, North America contributed 68% of ARR growth, with enterprise wins in healthcare and fintech—think integrations with Epic Systems and FIS platforms. EMEA accelerated to 45% YoY ARR growth, outpacing the company average, thanks to GDPR-compliant AI features that resonated with EU regulators and enterprises like a major German auto manufacturer scaling our anomaly detection modules. APAC, now 12% of total ARR, grew 52% YoY, but we're tempering expectations there due to currency headwinds from a strengthening USD and softer demand in Japan.

Key technical initiatives underpinning this growth include the GA launch of CloudForge AI Studio in July, which embeds generative AI capabilities directly into our core data orchestration engine. Early adopters are seeing 40-50% reductions in query optimization time via our AutoTune ML algorithms, driving upsell velocity. We've also deepened partnerships with hyperscalers: AWS Marketplace sales surged 60% QoQ, and our Azure-native certified status unlocked deals with two top-10 telcos.

Shifting to profitability: Our TTM FCF margin of 27% marks a 500 basis point improvement from the prior year and our best-ever quarterly print at 29% in Q3. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 28%, with gross margins steady at 82%—a testament to our shift toward higher-value seat-based pricing and reduced variable cloud costs via optimized GPU reservations. Operating expenses grew just 22% YoY, below revenue pace, as we realized efficiencies from our 2023 headcount optimization and automation of sales ops with our own platform. Capex remains low at 4% of revenue, focused on incremental data center capacity in Virginia and Frankfurt.

Our Rule of 40 has improved sequentially from 55% in Q3 FY23 to 62% today, even as we lap tougher comps. This puts us in elite company—comparable to ServiceNow's trajectory during their platform pivot or HubSpot's post-IPO scaling. Amid broader market conditions, SaaS multiples have compressed to 7-9x EV/ARR for growth names, but Rule of 40 leaders like ours trade at a premium.

Strategically, we're laser-focused on maintaining this balance. For FY24, we still expect full-year revenue of $520-525 million, or 33-34% growth, and FCF margins expanding to 26-28%. Into FY25, we'll lean into AI-driven product velocity—next up: federated learning for privacy-preserving analytics—and geographic diversification, targeting 15% of ARR from APAC by year-end.

Now, turning to free cash flow performance, which continues to be a hallmark of our SaaS model's scalability and operational discipline. For Q3 FY24, we generated $44 million in free cash flow, representing a robust 28% year-over-year increase from $34 million in Q3 last year. On a year-to-date basis through Q3, free cash flow reached $120 million, up 32% from the prior year. This translated to a Q3 free cash flow margin of 29% of revenue, expanding 450 basis points year-over-year and marking our eighth consecutive quarter of margin expansion.

Breaking down the key drivers, our ARR grew 36% year-over-year to $525 million, fueled by NRR of 118%—driven by upsell and cross-sell momentum in our AI-powered suite. Customers like a major Fortune 100 financial services firm expanded their seats by 40% after integrating our new generative AI features for real-time workflow automation. This recurring revenue profile converted to cash at an unlevered free cash flow margin of 27%, underscoring the high gross margins in our asset-light SaaS model.

Operationally, cash from operating activities came in strong, with improved working capital efficiency: DSO improved to 52 days from 58 days a year ago, thanks to our automated invoicing platform powered by Stripe integrations and enhanced credit checks. This generated additional cash compared to last year. On the payables side, DPO held steady at 65 days, reflecting disciplined vendor management amid cloud infrastructure costs, where we've locked in multi-year commitments with AWS and Azure to hedge against GPU price inflation tied to AI demand.

Sales and marketing efficiency was another standout, with CAC payback shrinking to 14 months from 17 months YoY. We're seeing payback under 12 months in North America for our enterprise segment, where we hit strong seat growth among large customers. This discipline allowed us to grow S&M spend below revenue pace—a testament to our Rule of 40 score of 62.

CapEx remained minimal at 4% of revenue, primarily for data center expansions in EMEA to support GDPR-compliant AI features. Regionally, North America contributed the majority of Q3 FCF, up strongly on hyperscaler deals. EMEA grew propelled by our data center launch and wins in regulated verticals. APAC was solidifying with localized AI models.

This FCF strength positions us to execute on high-return initiatives. We've deployed funds toward share repurchases, accretive to EPS, and earmarking capital for tuck-in M&A to accelerate NRR into the 120% range by FY25. Investments in serverless compute and zero-trust security will further deleverage opex, targeting FCF margins north of 30% long-term.

Finally, let's discuss our churn dynamics, which remain a cornerstone of our SaaS financial health here at CloudForge. In the Software/SaaS space, we track logo churn, gross revenue retention, and net revenue retention. Our playbook is laser-focused on maintaining high NRR, akin to leaders like Snowflake or ServiceNow.

For Q3 FY24, we delivered logo churn of 7.2% annualized—down 120 basis points from 8.4% in Q3 FY23 and sequentially flat from Q2's 7.3%. This puts us at the lower end of the spectrum for mid-market CRM/analytics platforms, outperforming peers like HubSpot but with room to close the gap to Salesforce. Gross revenue retention held steady at 92%, reflecting some pricing pressure but buffered by multi-year contracts. Most importantly, NRR expanded to 118% from 115% YoY, driven by 28% of customers expanding ACV by an average of 22%. This expansion cohort now represents 65% of our ARR, up from 58% last year.

Unpacking the key drivers of churn by customer tier: In the SMB segment (customers < $50K ACV, 62% of logos, 28% of ARR), this group drove 65% of logo churn at 11.5% annualized. Top culprits: budget constraints amid macroeconomic headwinds—like Fed rate hikes squeezing VC funding—mirroring Zoom or Asana. Specifically, 42% of SMB churn tied to cost optimization, with consolidation onto Microsoft Dynamics 365; onboarding friction accounted for 28%.

Mid-Market ($50K-$250K ACV, 28% of logos, 35% of ARR): Churn 6.8%, with competitive displacement at 35% to Pipedrive or Zoho CRM, and technical factors like API rate-limiting at 22%, exacerbated by usage-based pricing surprises.

Enterprise (>$250K ACV, 10% of logos, 37% of ARR): 3.2% churn, due to strategic pivots (18%) like EMEA telcos to Salesforce Einstein, and economic sensitivity (25%).

Regionally: North America (72% ARR) lowest at 6.5%, buoyed by Fortune 1000 adoption; EMEA (18% ARR) 9.1% from GDPR costs and Brexit; APAC (10% ARR) 8.4% from currency volatility and local competition.

Trends are encouraging: Sequential churn declined across segments, correlating to stabilizing SaaS multiples.

On mitigation, we've invested $45M in FY24 in proactive prevention, yielding 25% reduction in at-risk accounts. Our AI-powered ForgeGuard ML model flags risks 45 days early with 87% precision, analyzing 200+ signals, triggering 1,200 interventions YTD, saving $18M ARR.

Customer Success overhaul: 1:150 CSM ratio, proactive QBRs, Success Pods slashing early churn 40%. Product-led retention: freemium Essentials plan (+35% uptake), bundled add-ons boosting NRR 8 points, Kubernetes for 99.98% uptime.

Win-back: 22% reactivation recapturing $12M ARR; cross-sell Enterprise Suite. Regional tailoring: APAC local pricing, EMEA ESG modules.

We guide FY24 logo churn to 7.0% and NRR to 120%. Our Zero Churn by Design North Star fuels 15% organic growth.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first three quarters of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $520 to $525 million.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of CloudForge AI Studio on your overall growth?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks for the question, John. CloudForge AI Studio has been a game-changer for our growth trajectory. Since its GA launch in July, we've seen it contribute significantly to our 34% revenue growth this quarter. Early adopters, particularly in North America and EMEA, are expanding deployments rapidly—think 3x seat growth for some Fortune 100 clients—as it delivers 40-50% faster insights via AutoTune ML and zero-ETL integrations. This has directly boosted our NRR to 118%, with AI features driving 28% of expansions. Inbound pipeline from these capabilities is up 35%, reducing CAC, and it's accelerating our enterprise land-and-expand flywheel. We're just getting started, with more vertical AI agents on deck for FY25.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion?

Lisa Wong:
Great question, Emily. International markets now represent 30% of our ARR, up from 22% last year, and we're committed to doubling that to 40% by FY26. EMEA is our fastest grower at 45% YoY ARR, fueled by GDPR-ready AI features and wins like the German auto OEM—we're expanding our London data center and localizing for DACH with dedicated sales pods. In APAC, targeting 15% of ARR, we're countering currency headwinds with local pricing in JPY/AUD, JBS-100 compliance, and Mandarin/Japanese AI models; joint ventures in Japan/Australia drove 45% bookings growth despite yen issues. Key enablers: hyperscaler marketplaces (AWS/Azure up 60% QoQ), ABM for $500M+ enterprises, and Success Pods for 90-day onboarding. This balances our NA core while diversifying revenue.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Barclays.

David Lee:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, David. We've covered our churn playbook in detail earlier, but to summarize: Q3 logo churn improved to 7.2% annualized, NRR at 118%, with expansions from 28% of customers offsetting pressures. SMB budget cuts drove most volume, but our ForgeGuard AI predicts risks early (87% precision), saving $18M ARR via 1,200 interventions. CS overhauls, freemium tiers, API fixes, and regional tailoring—like EMEA ESG and APAC localization—have reduced at-risk conversions 25%. Win-back campaigns recapture 22% of lost logos. Guiding to 7.0% churn and 120% NRR for FY24, positioning us strongly.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
